newsitem.title: DENMARK: Berendsen, Ratin to honour Rentokil pledge.
newsitem.headline: Berendsen, Ratin to honour Rentokil pledge.

text.p: Danish holding company Sophus Berendsen said on Friday that its plan to split into two separately-listed companies would not affect a pledge to retain its holding in Britain's Rentokil Initial for at least five years.

The company on Thursday announced its intention to transfer a 32.2 percent stake in Rentokil Initial to a new holding company, Ratin A/S, while a restructured Sophus Berendsen would hold the remaining 3.6 percent and all other group activities.

"Ratin will retain its Rentokil shares for the five years from March 11, 1996, as we informed the Copenhagen Stock Exchange at the time," Berendsen managing director Hans Werdelin told Reuters, adding that Berendsen would do the same.
News of the split sent the group's share to a high of 1,030 crowns earlier on Friday, but by 1120 GMT it was down to 987.00, still well up on Thursday's closing 889.00.
